async_records.runtime_or_environment: browser and Node host APIs plus ECMAScript functions
async_records.problem_addressed: Represent async completion or event notification without blocking.
async_records.behavior_explained: A callback is a function value passed to an API and invoked later by that API or host environment. The surrounding call usually returns before the callback executes.
async_records.safe_pattern: Name callback boundaries, keep callback small, and ensure the outer function does not claim to return callback-produced data synchronously.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Returning a value from inside a callback and expecting the outer function to return it.
common_failure_modes: Outer function returns undefined or stale state
Exceptions occur outside expected synchronous control flow
Callback runs multiple times or never runs depending on API
diagnostic_questions: Which API invokes the callback and when?
Does the outer function return before the callback runs?
Can the callback run more than once?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Use a fake timer/event/source to prove ordering
Test zero, one, and multiple callback invocations

async_records.runtime_or_environment: primarily Node and callback-style host APIs
async_records.problem_addressed: Keep success and failure channels explicit for callback APIs.
async_records.behavior_explained: Many callback APIs report failure through an error argument or error event rather than throwing synchronously. Promise wrappers must translate that failure channel into rejection.
async_records.safe_pattern: Check the documented callback signature; handle error first where applicable; reject wrappers on error and resolve only on success.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Ignoring the error parameter or throwing inside an asynchronous callback expecting an outer try/catch to catch it.
diagnostic_questions: What is the documented error path?
Does a wrapper settle exactly once?
tests_or_evidence_needed: Stub API to call callback with error
Test success and error cannot both settle

async_records.problem_addressed: Schedule work after a delay or repeatedly.
async_records.behavior_explained: Timer APIs are host-provided. They schedule callbacks for later execution; delays are not precise guarantees of exact execution time, and ordering with other events/promises depends on host event loop behavior.
async_records.safe_pattern: Keep timer callbacks idempotent; clear timers when lifecycle ends; test with fake timers where appropriate.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Using setTimeout as a synchronization guarantee for network/DOM/stream completion.
diagnostic_questions: What condition is the timer standing in for?
Could callback run after state is invalid?

async_records.behavior_explained: EventEmitter-style APIs call listeners for named events. Error events and listener lifecycle are critical and current Node behavior must be verified for details.
async_records.safe_pattern: Handle error events, remove listeners when lifecycle ends, and document event ordering expectations.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Listening only for data/success events and ignoring error/close/end events.
diagnostic_questions: Which events mark data, completion, error, and close?

async_records.problem_addressed: Process large or incremental data without buffering everything.
async_records.behavior_explained: Streams emit or consume chunks over time and have lifecycle, backpressure, error, and completion semantics.
async_records.safe_pattern: Use lifecycle-aware helpers where available and verified; handle error and completion; choose object/binary/text mode deliberately.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Concatenating all chunks by default or assuming data event means complete data.
diagnostic_questions: Which event or promise indicates completion?

async_records.runtime_or_environment: browser workers and Node worker threads after current verification
async_records.problem_addressed: Move work across threads/process-like boundaries using messages.
async_records.behavior_explained: Worker APIs communicate through message events or ports. Values crossing the boundary follow host cloning/transfer rules; code does not share ordinary object identity.
async_records.safe_pattern: Define message schemas, correlate requests/responses, handle error/exit/termination, and verify current worker API details.
async_records.dangerous_pattern: Mutating an object after sending it and expecting the worker/main side to see the mutation.
diagnostic_questions: How are errors and exits reported?

pitfall_records.pitfall_or_failure_name: Browser API used in Node or Node API used in browser
pitfall_records.plain_language_description: Host-specific global or module is referenced in the wrong runtime.
pitfall_records.technical_description: ECMAScript core does not include DOM, fs, process, Buffer, or many other host APIs. Browsers and Node provide different host environments.
symptoms: fs not found in browser bundle
works in Jest but fails in browser
pitfall_records.root_cause_pattern: File role and execution runtime are not identified before review/refactor.
pitfall_records.minimal_example_shape: import fs from "fs" in frontend code or document.querySelector in Node script
pitfall_records.why_it_surprises_developers: All files are JavaScript, so environment differences are easy to miss.
checks_or_diagnostics: Search for browser and Node globals

pitfall_records.plain_language_description: Stream code handles chunks but not completion, errors, or backpressure.
pitfall_records.technical_description: Node streams are asynchronous data sources/sinks with data/end/error/close/finish/backpressure behavior. APIs evolve and should be verified for current Node.
pitfall_records.root_cause_pattern: Stream is treated as a complete buffer.
conditions_required: Only data handler or write calls present
pitfall_records.why_it_surprises_developers: Data chunks arrive over time and completion is a separate event/state.
prevention_or_mitigation: Use buffered read only for bounded input

pitfall_records.pitfall_or_failure_name: Child process or worker chosen without boundary plan
pitfall_records.plain_language_description: Parallel/external execution is added without accounting for messaging, lifecycle, security, and deployment support.
pitfall_records.technical_description: Node child processes and worker threads solve different problems and have different data, CPU, OS, security, and lifecycle behavior. Browser workers differ again.
pitfall_records.root_cause_pattern: Execution boundary choice is made before defining workload, data flow, and trust boundary.
pitfall_records.minimal_example_shape: exec(`tool ${userInput}`) or worker for small trivial task
pitfall_records.why_it_surprises_developers: The API can look like a performance shortcut while adding a new failure domain.
prevention_or_mitigation: Choose worker for CPU-bound JS; child process for trusted external program when deployment allows
Sanitize shell input or avoid shell

pitfall_records.pitfall_or_failure_name: Package or version mismatch changes runtime shape
pitfall_records.plain_language_description: Dependency update or package entry selection changes exports, module format, or behavior.
pitfall_records.technical_description: npm packages expose versions, entry points, exports, peer dependencies, and lifecycle scripts that affect what code runs.
pitfall_records.root_cause_pattern: Package metadata and lockfile are not reviewed with source code.
conditions_required: Package has conditional exports or peer dependencies
pitfall_records.minimal_example_shape: import {x} from "pkg" after package changed to default export or ESM-only
pitfall_records.why_it_surprises_developers: The application source did not change, but the dependency graph did.

pitfall_records.pitfall_or_failure_name: Apps Script runtime confused with browser or Node
pitfall_records.plain_language_description: Apps Script project code is reviewed as if every JavaScript file has the same APIs and lifecycle.
pitfall_records.technical_description: Apps Script server-side functions, HtmlService client HTML, triggers, Google services, quotas, scopes, and deployment behavior are Apps Script platform features outside the book.
pitfall_records.root_cause_pattern: Files are not classified by Apps Script runtime role and current docs are not checked.
conditions_required: Platform behavior claimed without current docs
pitfall_records.minimal_example_shape: Client HTML calls SpreadsheetApp directly or server .gs calls document.querySelector
pitfall_records.why_it_surprises_developers: All pieces are JavaScript-like, but they execute in different hosts with different services.
prevention_or_mitigation: Verify current Google docs for every service/trigger/quota/scope
Use explicit client/server message data shapes
checks_or_diagnostics: Which file runs in browser vs server?
Which service APIs and scopes are used?
What current docs prove quota/deployment behavior?
